claim: A mount body with `gc_fenced = true` is terminal for its `(server_uuid, writer_epoch)` incarnation; recovery must use a fresh `writer_epoch`.
`MountLeaseKeeper::claim` must refuse adoption of a fenced body when the observed UUID and epoch equal the current incarnation, and the caller must recover as a new incarnation.
The same-UUID/same-epoch refresh branch of `claimMount` must also refuse a fenced body; only a different epoch may reclaim it.
After `PreconditionFailed` in renewal or adoption, the mount-lease code re-reads the slot body and classifies the refusal by body contents rather than by token alone.
A foreign `server_uuid` causes a fail-closed refusal, while an own UUID with `gc_fenced` is a recoverable fence state and an own UUID with a newer unfenced epoch is a fail-closed supersession.

The generic `SingleWriterSlot` message `touched by a foreign writer` is reserved for an own-UUID, same-epoch, unfenced token violation; GC-fence recovery must report `fenced by GC after lease expiry` instead.
`prepareRenew` must be O(1) and use the last installed `retire_view.round()` acknowledgement plus `minActive()` without running the beat; the beat runs on a separate cadence.
Using a stale heartbeat acknowledgement for a renewal is conservative for the GC floor because it can only lower `min_ack` and delay graduation; lease expiry is the failure that must be avoided.

`Store::open` must wrap claim and keeper startup in a bounded retry loop; an adoption refusal classified as `fenced_by_gc` allocates a fresh epoch and retries, while foreign or superseded refusals abort.
`SingleWriterSlot::doTerminate` is a quiet no-op when `seq == 0`, because a keeper whose start never succeeded has nothing to release; double termination remains an exception.
The TLA+ mount model adds `GcFence`, splits adopt into GET and CAS steps, permits late renewal after expiry, and checks `FENCE-COSTS-EPOCH` plus eventual remount liveness.
The mount protocol invariant `FENCE-COSTS-EPOCH` requires that no write lands under a `(uuid, epoch)` incarnation after that incarnation has been fenced.
The mount-lease acceptance event is `mount_conflict` with `branch = "fenced_by_gc"` on the recoverable fence path.

The original P1 availability bug was a cold-open adoption race in which GC fencing landed between the non-atomic GET and PUT in `Store::open`, causing exit 49 with `touched while adopting our own mount slot`.

The TLA+ gate requires the old adopt path to violate `NoPermanentWedge` and same-epoch resurrection after a fence to violate `FenceCostsEpoch`; the fixed model must permit fence-to-new-epoch remount recovery.
The P3.1 design leaves beat cost and frequency tuning, structurally impossible in-degree recovery, GC liveness under contention, and first-open audit-event blindness out of scope.

The CAS night-campaign fix plan approved an instrument-first approach with four independent work packages; phases 2–4 do not depend on phase 1, although phase-2 audit events improve phase-3.1 diagnosis.
P1 was a chronic mount-lease race with about 26 occurrences on each node during the night; most self-healed by retry, but one S13 collision escalated to a permanent fail-closed exit 49.

P2 reported 116 `delete_pending blob recovered in-degree — structurally impossible under the ack floor (spared anyway, fail-closed)` events in a four-minute window on ch1; the root cause was unknown in the campaign.
P3 was a recurring `stageManifest: manifest ordinal collision`; one instance escaped retry to a foreground query as `LOGICAL_ERROR` 28 seconds after ch1 was mount-fenced.
P4 was an S3 multipart completion failure where 48 ETags were rejected after a writer kill, suggesting stale multipart-session reuse across incarnations.
P5 was GC round 31 stalling for about four hours under leader contention, with six of eight attempts reporting `manifests_deleted=0`, a 2:1 leadership skew, and chronic heartbeat acknowledgement lag.

P6 was a suspected S09 mutation carry-forward failure: the failing run had 2876 MiB pool growth and 34.5% S3 write errors versus 1.4 MiB and 12.5% on the passing rerun, leaving open whether write failure caused a full re-upload.
The campaign harness `gc_log` query still referenced removed columns `forgotten_on_delete` and `forgotten_absent`, causing 213 `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` errors per night and empty `gc_log` capture.
The harness `pool_shape` classifier was stale after per-server-tree relocation: S08 classified 858081 objects and 138 GB as `other` while `_manifests=0` for a 100k-part pool.
Container-cgroup `memory.peak` includes page cache and was measured at 5–21 times the ClickHouse-tracked peak, so memory verdicts based on it are unreliable.
The harness end-checkpoint `forced_gc_to_fixpoint` races the background GC tick, producing `GC round raced background tick (ABORTED)` and causing seven of fifteen runs to end inconclusive.
The campaign harness hid sustained 10–20% S3 read-error rates because verdict tables asserted operation counts but not error rates.
CAS had no `CurrentMetrics` or `AsynchronousMetrics` gauges; its introspection surface consisted of historical log tables and monotone counters.
Mount and lease state, including slot holder, renewal health, and fencing, was visible outside `err.log` only after adding the proposed introspection package.

The planned `system.content_addressed_mounts` table exposes one point-in-time row per srid with `disk_name`, `srid`, `server_uuid`, `writer_epoch`, `expires_at_ms`, `min_active`, `observed_gc_round`, `gc_fenced`, and `state`.

The phase-4 GC optimization skips unchanged namespaces so an idle round approaches O(servers) reads and a small-delta round costs O(delta), with a mandatory TLA+ proof that owner-removal events are never skipped.

With `mount_lease_ttl_ms = 30000` and `mount_renew_period = 10000`, 20 rapid kill-restart cycles did not reach the 45-second fence threshold; lease collisions require renewals blocked beyond `ttl + ttl/2`.

The observed `gc_fence_out` preserves the expired mount's own `server_uuid` and fences it by setting `gc_fenced = true`, so the apparent foreign writer is the GC leader performing a legitimate fence-out.

`MountLeaseKeeper` renewal can block beyond the 30-second TTL because `prepareRenew` runs `Store::refreshViewForBeat`, which may wait for exclusive `view_gate` access and perform retired-view S3 reads.

When a blocked renewal resumes after GC fenced the expired slot, its token-guarded `putOverwrite` receives `PreconditionFailed` and the old code reports the misleading `touched by a foreign writer — failing closed, never re-minting` message.

The cold-open path has no retry around the GET→PUT adoption window, so a fence landing there throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` `touched while adopting our own mount slot` during metadata load and leaves the container down with exit 49.
If GC fences a fresh lease before the adopt GET, the old `claimMount` and `claim` checks can resurrect a fenced incarnation under the same epoch, contradicting the terminal-incarnation rule.

A fence-recovery implementation must classify same-UUID fenced bodies as recoverable, decouple the beat from the renewal deadline, retry cold-open claim/adopt, and make `doTerminate` with `seq == 0` a no-op.

A read-only `ca_ro` disk over the same pool and `server_root_id` as writable `ca` causes MergeTree part discovery to find parts on both disks and fail restart with `UNKNOWN_DISK` and `ASYNC_LOAD_WAIT_FAILED` when `ca_ro` is absent from policy `ca`.

The stand workaround for the `ca_ro` restart issue is to remove `ca_ro` from server `config.d`, mount it through standalone `/etc/clickhouse-server/fsck-only.xml`, and invoke fsck with that configuration.

The underlying `ca_ro` same-pool part-discovery interaction remains a product prod-gate item even after the default stand workaround; other stand configurations still require the workaround before restart scenarios.
`ca-gc-dryrun` proposed 132 blobs as deletable in S18 even though fsck classified them reachable and real GC spared them, demonstrating reachability divergence for frozen or shadow-referenced data.

A rejected `ALTER TABLE s19_src MOVE PARTITION 2 TO DISK 'default'` correctly raised `Code:479 UNKNOWN_DISK`, but two `CasRootCas` operations occurred before validation, so the move was not perfectly atomic even though fsck remained clean.

The S24 replica-agreement failure was a harness timing issue: the check ran before replication converged because it lacked `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA`, while a post-run check showed identical 280-row replicas and checksum `8663329780789566770`.

Across S18, S25, and S26, `ca-gc-dryrun` over-proposed reachable blobs while real GC kept them and fsck reported `dangling=0`; this is a systematic dryrun reachability defect across shadow, non-Atomic, and verbatim-churn roots.

S30 initially measured `CasRootGet` growth from 75 to 190 across 30 create/drop cycles despite no live tables, but the later S34 correction attributed the apparent F5 defect to sampling reclaim backlog instead of steady-state discovery.
At steady state after driving GC to an idle deferred round, S34 measured zero discovery `CasRootGet` operations for iteration counts from 5 through 40 and flat `root_dirs = 2`.

S35 rapid same-name rotation preserved the resurrect invariant: no dangling content, reclaimable residual drained to zero, no revived condemned object, and the final recreated table remained queryable with replica agreement.
Before the cache-over-CA fix, a `<type>cache</type>` disk over CA failed closed at `IDisk::startup` with code 48 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` because the generic cache metadata wrapper hid the CA write path.
The cache-over-CA startup diagnostic explicitly names the `ca_cache` wrapper and recommends using the content-addressed disk directly in the storage policy until the combination is wired.
S12 ten-replica shared-pool validation showed byte-identical convergence, `CasBlobBodyPutAvoided=40`, and `dangling=0` under concurrent inserts.
Under S22's injected 503, 429, slow, and reset faults, 336 faults produced zero workload errors, replica agreement, and `dangling=0`; bounded retries absorbed the faults.

Under S27 duplicate-key and dropped-continuation-token LIST anomalies, GC tolerated 40 perturbed LISTs with zero round errors, replica agreement, `dangling=0`, and dropped-content reclamation; unstable listings increased `CasRootGet` from 74 to 1373 as GC conservatively re-read.
A full-scale S13 run wedged during quiesce because RustFS returned `503 Service Unavailable`, leaving merges at `progress=1.0` and causing no-timeout `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA` to block.
The S13 fitted rerun reproduced the same wedge with 8 KiB payloads and 459 GB free, disproving near-disk-full and payload size as the primary cause.

The refined F2 root cause is RustFS issue `rustfs#3231`: overwriting objects larger than 128 KiB in an unversioned bucket leaks prior data directories, and metacache walks then time out and produce LIST storms and 503s.
The S13 merge-finalize retry path re-uploaded blobs on every attempt during persistent 503s, growing the pool by 47 GB in eight minutes after the workload stopped.
The P3.1 fence-recovery cycle recovered a fenced ch1 mount in about two seconds as `writer_epoch=2`, `seq=1`, `gc_fenced=0`, and `state=live`, with no post-kill foreign-writer or exit-49 lines.

The dev-scale S13 smoke passed all safety checks, including `fsck dangling=0`, replica agreement, bounded abandoned-precommit residual, no failed GC rounds, and `dryrun ⊆ unreachable`; its lone inconclusive result was only an observability gate.

The full-scale S13 chaos run reached ch1 `writer_epoch=26` after approximately 24 clean fence recoveries with zero exit-49 wedge and zero foreign-writer message in the run window, despite later RustFS quiesce failure.

Merge-heavy full-scale CAS scenarios must remain below the RustFS `rustfs#3231` overwrite-churn threshold or use a fixed RustFS or fault-proxy stand; dev or reduced-round runs are the operational fallback.

The dangling-precommit fix uses a fold-side, watermark-keyed force-Read: `ShardCoverage` records the minimal live precommit binding, and `computeDiscoverDecisions` overrides `Skip` when that precommit is provably dead.
The new `ShardCoverage` fields are `has_live_precommit`, `min_live_precommit_writer_epoch`, and `min_live_precommit_build_sequence`, and they round-trip through the fold-seal codec.

`isPrecommitDead(uint64_t writer_epoch, uint64_t build_sequence, const MountLease & w)` must be shared by reclaim and discover paths; a future epoch is live, an older epoch is dead, and an equal epoch is dead only when the retired sentinel or `min_active > build_sequence` applies.
`ProfileEvents::CasGcPrecommitRevisitForced` counts forced re-folds of token-stable ref-shards whose watermark-dead live precommit must be reclaimed.
The force-Read fix must preserve `Skip` for a shard with no live precommit or a live-but-not-yet-dead precommit, and must be idempotent after the removal changes the shard token.
The dangling-precommit regression scenario is S30, whose `no unbounded leftovers` verdict must show no `_manifests` leak after the fix.

A content-static ref-shard can permanently orphan a manifest when an abandoned precommit remains in its journal: token-diff `Skip` prevents `reclaimAbandonedPrecommit` from running after the watermark later proves the precommit dead.

The force-Read guard is self-terminating: reclaim appends a removal, the shard token changes, the next round reads normally, and the shard becomes `Skip`-eligible after coverage no longer contains a live precommit.

`ShardCoverage` stores the lexicographically minimal `{writer_epoch, build_sequence}` among live precommit bindings, stamps it on every Read visit, and carries it through Skip and durable fold-seal restart.
The force-Read guard never reclaims a live precommit: a build at or above the floor, a future epoch, or a missing watermark is spared, and `Build::promote` remains a fail-closed backstop.
Force-Read is strictly more reading than Skip and therefore cannot under-count in-degree; each abandoned precommit adds at most one forced revisit at the round its build sequence crosses the floor.
A lost R5 round CAS may repeat the same force-Read and exact precommit removal, but the fold cursor advances past the removal transition so the `-1` is folded only once.
The `SkipParksDeadPrecommit` TLA+ bug configuration must violate `LiveDeadPrecommitReclaimed`, while the fix configuration with watermark-dead force-Read must satisfy it under weak fairness.

A sweep-only defense that makes `activeManifestKeys` judge precommits dead was deferred because it would delete the manifest body without releasing the precommit's pinned blob edges; the fold-side fix is required.

The resurrect-reupload fix keys blob condemnation on `(hash, current token)` instead of only on the hash, and re-condemns a current token when a touched hash has net in-degree zero and a prior retired token differs.
The resurrect supersede produces one retired entry per hash, drops the stale token entry, preserves hash order, and commits the replacement through the existing R5 round CAS.
A resurrect supersede emits `blob_retire_replaced` and increments `CasGcRetireReplaced`.
The resurrect fix must not condemn a current blob with `cur_edges > 0`; that case remains on the existing `spared` or recovery branch.
When token A was condemned and a writer re-uploaded token B at the same blob key, exact-token deletion of A found B and no-op'd, while the hash-keyed fold failed to condemn B, leaving B orphaned.
A fresh upload is condemned only when the hash has been referenced, the current object exists, and its folded current in-degree is zero; never-referenced uploads are not condemned.
The resurrect-reupload rule is idempotent under R5 retry because it is a pure function of the edge stream and current HEAD, and an existing entry for the current token is not reset or duplicated.
Writers consult `store->retireView().isCondemnedToken(hash, token)`; recording the current resurrected token B as condemned makes a later dedup hit re-upload instead of adopting B.
The resurrect-replaced repair adds one HEAD only for a touched condemned transition; quiescent graduation through `settleRetiredBelow` takes no additional HEAD.

The observability follow-up must make the supersede token peek side-effect-free and carry the old token so exactly one `blob_retire_replaced` event records the repair without a second `blob_retire` or `CasGcRetiredCondemned` increment.
For a content-addressed disk, `DiskObjectStorage::wrapWithCache` reuses the CA metadata storage and wraps only the object storage with `CachedObjectStorage`.
CA metadata `startup()` and `shutdown()` are idempotent, allowing the base disk and cache disk to share one CA mount and one lease when they reuse the same metadata storage.
Under cache-over-CA, immutable content-hash blobs are read through `CachedObjectStorage`, while refs, manifests, GC, and writes use the CA metadata storage's raw uncached object-storage pointer.

The cache-over-CA design rejects making the generic cache wrapper impersonate CA concrete types and rejects peeling wrappers at every dynamic-cast site; direct CA metadata reuse has the smaller blast radius.
The CA cache disk shares the base disk's metadata-bound disk identity for GC scheduling and `system.content_addressed_log` attribution, so two disk names correspond to one GC identity.
The file cache is write-around rather than write-through: the first read after upload can miss once, then immutable content-hash data is cached without an invalidation hazard.

The cache-over-CA integration test demonstrates a cold scan with positive `CachedReadBufferReadFromSourceBytes`, a warm scan with at least ten times fewer source bytes, positive `CachedReadBufferReadFromCacheBytes`, and populated `system.filesystem_cache`.
The cache-over-CA test policy is named `cas_cache`, with CA disk `disk_ca_s3` wrapped by `disk_ca_s3_cache` using `<type>cache</type>` and a one-billion-byte local cache.
Write-through caching and caching the refs/manifests control plane are out of scope; immutable-blob write-around is the intended design.
The observability package emits `ManifestPut` after `Build::stageManifest` writes a body and emits `PrecommitRemoved` after `Build::abandon` removes a precommit binding.
`ManifestPut` records `object_kind = Manifest`, the owning namespace, `manifestRefDebugString(id.ref)`, the body token, and reason `stageManifest: part-manifest body written`.

`PrecommitRemoved` records `object_kind = Root`, the target namespace and ref, `manifestRefDebugString(precommit_manifest)`, and reason `abandon: precommit binding removed`; GC-side removals remain `PrecommitReclaim` events.
`ManifestExpand`, `ManifestRetire`, and `ManifestStrip` are obsolete dead enum entries from the removed Merkle layer and must be deleted rather than implemented.
The event sink is best-effort and does not participate in CAS decisions or block them, so adding lifecycle events does not change protocol safety.
`clickhouse-disks ca-inspect <key>` is a read-only command that dispatches CA bucket keys by `Layout` and renders decoded objects as human-readable JSON.

`ca-inspect` recognizes `cas/refs`, `cas/manifests`, `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount`, `gc/state`, fold seals, retired sets, and blob envelope headers; unknown keys fail closed with an error listing recognized layouts.
`ca-inspect` renders `u128`, token, and hash fields as lowercase hexadecimal and reports decode failures rather than emitting partial or guessed output.
`ca-inspect` requires a read-only-opened content-addressed object-storage disk and performs no CAS, delete, or mutation operation.
The manifest/precommit audit acceptance test requires one `manifest_put` and one `precommit_removed` row for the corresponding lifecycle operations.

The side-effect-free supersede peek must cause exactly one `blob_retire_replaced` event with `detail["superseded_token"]`, one `CasGcRetireReplaced` increment, and no accompanying `blob_retire` or `CasGcRetiredCondemned` increment.
The unit-testable `caInspectToJson` interface has signature `String caInspectToJson(const Layout & layout, const String & key, std::string_view bytes)`.

Before the observability package, `system.content_addressed_log` could not show a manifest body birth or writer-side precommit removal, so a precommit created and never removed required raw-object decoding to diagnose.
Before `ca-inspect`, diagnosing a CA bucket object required an ephemeral `mc` container, an `od` hexdump, and hand parsing of protobuf or custom binary data even though decoders already existed.
